chapter: Back to the horn: house sessions
title: Putting the horn aside, Johnny Cutrera and starting sessions again
summary: His son damaged the horn, he loaned it to Cutrera, then took it back and began sessions at home.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: Uh...I was gonna ask you about something else too... You left Brindley and you said you quit...did you stop playing entirely? Yeah...I quit entirely... You just...put your horn aside...

Put my horn aside...and got away from it...and the next time I saw my horn... My little boy...Albert was about...3 or 4 years old...and he had it...I put one of the...the middle key...uh...key-eye...and jammed a clothespin in there... So I had to send the horn to the factory...and have it done over...I did have it gone over...and...after I got it back...I loaned it to Johnny Cutrera... Johnny used my horn for maybe...2 or 3 years...he had my horn...
When was this...about when you were...

Well...when Johnny was playing...Johnny Cutrera was...he was playing in them...diam...diam...diam...diam...diam dance joints...on...the...fine...and those kind of places... Uh-huh... You know Johnny don't you?
Yeah...I know him...I used to hear him during the war...at the puppy house...

Yeah...and...I don't know what made me...wanna play again...so I got my horn back from Johnny...and I start...I believe I started giving him sessions at my house...you know... I got my house...I believe you came to a few of them... Sure...yeah... I gave a few sessions at the house...started giving those sessions at the house...till they got too big...I had to cut it out...man... This fella didn't invite that fella...and before you knew it...I had 40...30...40 people out there...
